judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "has contributed or is deemed to have contributed" leaves it uncertain whether any actual payment was made, and the whole operative content is delegated to Schedule A, which carries the plainly erroneous figure "$00,001.00" for LSB. That is both a lexical ambiguity ("deemed") and a mechanical error in the incorporated amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A's contribution figures sit awkwardly against Section 6.8(iii), which contemplates reimbursing DMSA for "initial capital contributions," and against Section 4.3(i)'s pro-rata return rule; the 49%/51% Percentage Interests do not track the stated dollar amounts. A dispute over what LSB actually contributed would require reconciling these provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "This Agreement and the rights of the parties hereunder shall be interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of Maine" is limited to interpretation and "rights hereunder," leaving open whether it reaches non-contractual (tort, fiduciary, statutory) claims between the members. That scope question is a recognised source of argument over the same words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.7 imports the Maine Business Corporation Act standard, consistent with Maine law, but the Company's principal place of business is in Massachusetts (Section 2.5) and LSB is a Massachusetts resident, so a party could argue the clause does not displace Massachusetts law for extra-contractual claims. No square contradiction, but there is friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" plus "any transfer restrictions contained in this Agreement" is a sweeping override whose reach against specific consent requirements is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It would let the Board override Section 14.3's requirement of all Members' written consent to a pledge and Section 16.6's right of first refusal, which are member protections not Board matters.
judgments.clause_name: Section 16.8 Waivers of Restrictions on Transfer

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Delivery methods and the receipt rule are stated definitely, though the list of permitted methods is joined disjunctively without a clear requirement to use any one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.5 and Schedule A addresses; no other provision prescribes a different notice regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is confusingly constructed ("shall not prevent a subsequent act ... from having the effect of an original violation"), but the anti-waiver intent is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.3 and with the express waiver powers in Sections 16.5 and 16.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative-remedies language, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and conventional, with an express "to the extent permitted by this Agreement" qualifier on assigns.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Articles XIV and XVI restricting assignment, and with Section 17.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely mechanical construction rule; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its statement that all references to Sections correspond to provisions of this Agreement is embarrassed by the non-existent Sections 6.9, 16.9, 16.10 and 16.11 cited elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability language; the stray period mid-sentence is immaterial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(ii) and 13.1 referring to counterpart execution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "pertaining to the subject matter hereof" is the usual formulation; its outer edge is arguable but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision preserves side agreements, and the Agreement contains no schedule of surviving arrangements, so it fits the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires unanimous vote plus a writing executed by all Members; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) says revisions to Schedule A — which fixes contributions, Percentage Interests and votes — are not amendments, carving a significant exception out of this unanimity requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Nothing expressed or implied shall be construed to confer upon any Person, except the Members and Managers, any rights or remedies" is clear in form, though it omits a subject and does not say under what instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes Officers, Affiliates, employees and agents, yet Sections 12.4 and 12.5 confer indemnification and advancement rights on all "Covered Persons," a broader class — a real tension.
judgments.clause_name: Section 17.11 No Implied Rights or Remedies
